title: Skip casks whose app belongs to another user in a run without sudo
notes: On a Mac with Homebrew shared between accounts (office Mac, user oficina, apps in /Applications owned by cristiandeluxe) a --scheduled run on 2026-11-24 failed every cask upgrade at 'Using sudo to gain ownership' and left 34 app backup copies (about 15 GB) in /opt/homebrew/Caskroom; the next manual run then failed with 'It seems there is already an App at'.

Local uncommitted patch in plugins/homebrew.sh on the office Mac (~/src/RocketUpdater): cask_app_needs_sudo + a skip with echo_warning when SUDO_AVAILABLE is not true. format, lint and test-regressions pass. Needs review and a commit upstream.
done_when: The change is committed upstream or replaced by an equivalent, and a sudo-less run leaves no .app directories in the Caskroom
result: Skip casks whose app belongs to another user in a run without sudo
evidence: plugins/homebrew.sh cask_app_needs_sudo skips the cask with a warning when SUDO_AVAILABLE is not true; tests/plugins/homebrew-pinned-foreign-cask.sh GREEN and RED without the change; scripts/test-regressions.sh passes
